commit.message:
🐛 fix(schema): retain JSON value key metadata

Keep Schema.Json a Codec<Json> subtype with required readonly decoded and encoded keys and a precise rebuild type. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

Validation: pnpm check; pnpm test-types JsonSchema (16 tests, 60 assertions over TS 5.9 and 6); targeted runtime tests (2); targeted oxlint and dprint.

Co-Authored-By: Codex <noreply@openai.com>
fix(effect): honor plateau budgets after flaky candidates
fix(effect): preserve Fuzz regressions and report unusable runs

feat(effect): confirm Fuzz findings and report flaky ones

Review round 1 (Astra finding 11, and the double confirmation that the
unresolved Struct finding showed was needed).

- Before a finding is reported, its final input (and schedule) is evaluated
  once more. A finding that does not fail with the same signature is a
  FlakyFinding carrying both outcomes (`failure`, `recheck`). Search findings,
  saved-failure regressions and replay tokens are all confirmed.
- Reports: `Falsified` holds confirmed findings plus `flaky`; a run with only
  flaky failures is a new `Flaky` report, never `Falsified`. Only confirmed
  findings count toward maxFindings. formatReport marks flaky ones FLAKY.
- Fuzz.run, Fuzz.runTarget, FUZZ.md and the @effect/vitest README state the
  property contract: same outcome for the same input, and never mutate the
  input, with an example of copying first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(effect): frame Fuzz corpus fields, validate tokens, keep store and shrink defects typed

Review round 1 (Astra findings 3, 8, 9, 10, 12).

- Corpus format version 2 writes revision, signature, codec and value as JSON
  string literals: a codec value with a newline or a field-looking line no
  longer truncates on load and turns a regression green. Version 1 files load.
- Entries reject duplicate fields, a null-prototype other than true/false, a
  bias outside 2..6, and failures without a signature.
- Replay tokens must hold nine fields of the right types and a failure
  signature; a "Passed" or "Limited" token is a Configuration error, not a
  Falsified report. Empty error names become "Object" so every signature is
  accepted back.
- Store calls and replay path-following sit behind defect boundaries: a store
  that throws or dies is FuzzError("Corpus"), a dying lazy shrink pull while
  following a path is FuzzError("Generation").
- Without a store the codec is never called.
- The hash test pins the key of the committed example failure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(vitest): replay fuzz failures under their execution driver; hash corpus directories

Review round 1 (Astra findings 1, 2, 4, 12).

- A plain run keeps `fuzz.execution`, so a race saved by a simulation session
  replays under the simulation and fails the next run (it passed before).
- Under `it.effect.fuzz` with an execution driver, the driver's Clock and
  Scheduler are provided inside the test services, so sleeps and timeouts run
  in virtual time instead of on TestClock (they were reported as Deadlock).
  The plain-run random check runs 100 executions under the driver.
- Corpus directories are the readable id plus 16 hex digits of its SHA-256:
  "parse: x" and "parse x" no longer share failures; "", "." and ".." stay
  inside the corpus. The committed example fixture moves to its new directory.
- Registration tests count callback invocations and register expected failures
  through `it.fails`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(effect): bound FuzzSimulation timer loops, keep nanosecond time, finish finalizers

Review round 1 (Astra findings 5, 6, 7).

- Timer wakes count toward maxSteps, including each wake in an equal-deadline
  batch, so a loop of sleeps ends as Limited instead of pumping forever.
- The step limit is checked before a task leaves the queue.
- The driver yields its own fiber every 4096 steps, so interrupting a fuzz run
  stops a long evaluation; an interrupted run releases the world first.
- Virtual time is integer nanoseconds; sub-millisecond sleeps no longer throw
  in the BigInt clock accessors and become Died findings.
- After a deadlock or step limit, finalizers run with another maxSteps; if they
  are still running after that, the driver dies (FuzzError "Execution") rather
  than reporting a finding with resources half released.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(vitest): document it.effect.fuzz; refresh the example saved failure

The example fixture keeps its key and value; its note line now shows the
codec text instead of a double-encoded string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(effect): add FuzzSimulation for schedule and virtual-time fuzzing

FuzzSimulation.execution() runs each Fuzz evaluation in a closed world:
one priority/FIFO queue for every dispatcher, slice lengths read from a
schedule tape that the fuzzer mutates and shrinks toward zero, and a
virtual clock. A property left with nothing runnable is a Deadlock
finding. Finds a lost-update race that checkEffect passes at 10,000 runs
and replays it identically 1,000 times.

Parent energy now comes only from span, observation and provider
features when any exist; the magic-number benchmark goes from 2 of 5
seeds to 8 of 8.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(vitest): add it.effect.fuzz and it.fuzz with a saved failure corpus

A plain run replays the failures a fuzz session saved beside the test and
then runs the usual random check. EFFECT_FUZZ selects tests for a search
that saves findings to __fuzz__/<file>/<test>/ through a node:fs store.
Adds FUZZ.md and an example test whose committed failure replays.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(effect): add Fuzz, feedback-guided fuzzing over Arbitrary

Fuzz.run and Fuzz.target/runTarget drive the existing Arbitrary generators
from a mutable word tape, keep inputs that produce new span, cause,
structural or observation feedback, shrink each distinct failure with the
existing shrink trees while keeping its signature, and save failures to a
corpus store before and after shrinking. Arbitrary and checkEffect are
unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
